q: 1. ISI has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: As per Indian Standards Institution (ISI/BIS) practice, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is specified and evaluated at 28 days of curing.

q: 2. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening refers to the process where the cement paste, after setting, continues to gain strength over time through ongoing hydration.

q: 3. A construction joint is provided where
options: the member is supported by other member
explain: Construction joints are best located where structural actions (bending moment and shear) are minimal, or where the member is supported by another member — all of these are valid locational criteria.

q: 4. Horizontal construction joint in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls can be provided at any of these convenient locations — soffit, floor, or window sill level — depending on the pour sequence, so all apply.

q: 5. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the types of vibrator used is
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are inserted directly into the concrete mass and are best suited for compacting large sections of mass concrete.

q: 6. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in walls are conveniently located at floor levels, lintel soffit levels, and window sill levels, as these are natural break points in the wall's structural continuity.

q: 7. For walls, columns and vertical faces of all structural members, the formwork is generally removed after
explain: Vertical formwork on walls, columns, and similar faces that carry no load can typically be removed relatively early, within about 24 to 48 hours, since these surfaces are non-load-bearing during curing.

q: 8. High increase in temperature ......... the strength of concrete.
explain: Excessively high curing/placing temperatures accelerate early hydration but result in a weaker, more porous microstructure, ultimately decreasing long-term concrete strength.

q: 9. Which of the following types of concrete mixers is most commonly used in precast concrete factories?
explain: Pan type mixers, which provide intensive and uniform mixing suited to stiff/low-slump mixes, are most commonly used in precast concrete factory production.

q: 10. Curing period required is minimum for the concrete using
explain: Rapid hardening cement gains strength very quickly, so the minimum curing period required for concrete made with it is the shortest among the options.

q: 11. Segregation in concrete results in
explain: Segregation of concrete leads to a range of defects including honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling — so all of these are consequences.

q: 12. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: The concrete gains strength due to hydration of cement
The concrete cured at a temperature below 23°C, gains strength up to 28 days
The concrete does not set at freezing point
The strength of concrete increases with its age
explain: All four statements are correct: hydration drives strength gain, curing temperature and duration affect the rate of gain, hydration effectively stops at freezing point, and strength continues to increase with the age of the concrete.

q: 13. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of ingredients in the correct proportions ensures the concrete achieves economy, workability, and the intended strength simultaneously.

q: 14. High increase in temperature
options: Has no effect on the strength of concrete
explain: A high increase in curing/ambient temperature accelerates early hydration but leads to a more porous, less uniform microstructure and rapid moisture loss, ultimately reducing the long-term strength of concrete.

q: 15. For concreting tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete in confined and elongated spaces like tunnel linings, where other methods are impractical.

q: 16. Curing a concrete for long period ensures better
explain: Extended curing periods allow more complete hydration, which improves volume stability, strength, water-tightness, and overall durability of concrete all together.

q: 17. The breaking up and remixing of concrete that has layers to set is called
explain: Resetting is the process of breaking up concrete that has already begun to set in layers and remixing it, typically done when placement is delayed beyond the initial setting time.

q: 18. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
explain: Uneven compaction leaves some parts under-compacted, resulting in porosity, a non-homogeneous structure, and consequently reduced strength throughout the member.

q: 19. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
explain: Expansion joints are typically provided in long concrete structures once the length exceeds about 45m, to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction movements.

q: 20. The internal dimensions of a ware house are 15m x 5.6m, and the maximum height of piles is 2.70 m. The maximum number of bags to be stored in two piles, are
explain: Based on the given warehouse dimensions (15m x 5.6m) with a maximum stacking height of 2.70 m, divided into two piles, the calculated maximum storage capacity works out to 3000 bags.

q: 21. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is:
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are best suited for compacting large volumes of mass concrete by inserting them directly into the concrete.

q: 22. After 28 days concrete acquires
explain: While 28-day strength is the standard reference for design, concrete at this stage has actually already gained more than 80% of its long-term ultimate strength.

q: 23. No shrinkage occurs if the concrete is placed in a relative humidity of
explain: At 100% relative humidity, there is no moisture loss from the concrete to the surrounding environment, so drying shrinkage does not occur.

q: 24. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching ensures the correct mix proportions, which in turn governs the strength, workability, and durability of the resulting concrete — all of these depend on it.

q: 25. In the batching of materials, the ingredients should be measured to a tolerance (as a percentage of batch quantity) of
explain: As per standard practice, concrete batching ingredients should be measured within a tolerance of ±3% of the specified batch quantity to ensure acceptable mix accuracy.

q: 26. During manufacture of concrete minimum period for which mixing is done in mixer for manufactured/crushed aggregate is (IS 456:2000)
explain: As per IS 456:2000, for concrete made with manufactured (crushed) aggregate, the minimum mixing period specified in the mixer is 2 minutes, since crushed aggregates require more thorough mixing.

q: 27. For concreting of tunnel lining, the concrete is transported by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete into confined spaces such as tunnel linings, where access is restricted.

q: 28. The concrete mixers are normally classified on the basis of
options: the technique of discharging the mixed concrete
explain: Concrete mixers are classified based on multiple criteria simultaneously - their discharge mechanism, batch capacity, and number of drums.

q: 29. The diameter of pipeline used for transportation of concrete by pumps should not exceed
explain: As given in this text, the pipeline diameter used for pumping concrete should not exceed about 30 cm.

q: 30. To prevent segregation of concrete, the concrete should not be thrown from a height of more than
explain: To avoid segregation, freshly mixed concrete should not be dropped or thrown from a height greater than about 1 m.

q: 31. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag for 50kg cement are
options: 70 liters of sand 120 liters of aggregates
70 kg of sand 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 210 liters of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix by volume with a standard 50 kg (35-litre volume) cement bag, the proportional quantities work out to 105 litres of sand (3 x 35) and 210 litres of aggregates (6 x 35).

q: 32. The process of hardening the concrete mix by keeping its surface moist for a certain period is called
explain: Curing is defined as maintaining adequate moisture at the concrete surface for a specified period to allow proper hydration and hardening.

q: 33. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
explain: Concrete placing is preferably carried out at a moderate temperature of around 27 ± 2°C, which is favourable for proper hydration and setting without excessive heat or cold-related issues.

q: 34. Vertical sides of column may be stripped after
explain: Since vertical column sides are non-load-bearing formwork, they can be stripped relatively early, typically within 1 to 2 days.

q: 35. The drying of concrete after casting results in
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete, the paste loses volume, causing drying shrinkage.

q: 36. Steam curing is used in
explain: Steam curing is primarily employed in the mass production of precast concrete elements, where accelerated strength gain is needed to allow rapid mould turnover in factory settings.

q: 37. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: there should not be any loss of cement from the charged drum of the mixer
cement should be mixed for at least one minute
10% of water is placed in the rotating drum before adding dry material
10% of water is added after placing the other ingredients in the drum
explain: All these are standard good-practice requirements for charging and mixing a concrete mixer, so the combined statement 'all of the above' is correct.

q: 38. The final operation of finishing floors, is known
explain: Trowelling is carried out last, after floating, to produce a smooth, dense, and hard surface finish on concrete floors.

q: 39. Horizontal construction joins in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls are conventionally placed at soffit level, window sill level, and floor level, since these are natural break points in the pour.

q: 40. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature & time
explain: Maturity is a concept that combines the effects of curing temperature and time (the temperature-time factor), used to estimate strength gain, rather than simply age.

q: 41. For concreting tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: Pumping is used to transport concrete into confined spaces like tunnel linings where direct access for other transport methods is restricted.

q: 42. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete during drying, the paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink.

q: 43. Separation of coarse aggregates from mortar during transportation is known as
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation of the coarser aggregate particles from the finer mortar/paste fraction of a concrete mix, often occurring during transport or over-vibration.
